newsitem.title: USA: Rubin-deficit reduction critical for strong growth.
newsitem.headline: Rubin-deficit reduction critical for strong growth.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said a reduced budget deficit is vital for a healthy U.S. economy in the long run and stressed the importance of non-partisan cooperation to balance the budget.

"And just as deficit reduction has been the critical factor in the current favorable economic conditions, so is it critical to a strong long-term economy," Rubin said in a prepared speech he present later at an event sponsored by the Society of American Business Editors and Writiers.

In the speech, Rubin underscored that Democratic and Republican parties "should and can work together" and that the tone of budget negotiations has been more "constructive and positive" than in the past.
Rubin said developing countries are becoming increasingly important to the economic well-being of the United States.
"They (developing nations) account for 40 percent of U.S. exports -- and those exports are increasing at a pace that is faster by two-thirds the rate of exports to developed countries," he said.

Regarding trade relations, Rubin said the Clinton administration will be working with Congress to "establish the appropriate negotiating authority for future trade agreements, and to maintain Most Favored Nation status -- that is, a normal trade relationship -- with China."
